info.title: OpenSMS Customer API
info.description: Customer API contract for the OpenSMS service. Authentication, messaging, batching, wallet, compliance, analytics, webhooks, numbers, OTP, and public status handlers are implemented in the API binary.

get.summary: Operational Prometheus scrape on the optional dedicated listener
get.description: Not served on the customer API port. Enable the separate metrics listener explicitly. Non-loopback listeners require their configured bearer token. Measurements are operational and are not financial accounting.

Repeated identical PUTs do not duplicate audit/events. This endpoint configures consent and performs no external charge.

The pinned provider must exist with an active status and is only preferred when eligible; it never bypasses eligibility. Existing queued messages retain their accepted routing policy. API keys cannot change this setting.

post.summary: Accept a current legal version for the authenticated member
post.description: Requires active membership in the explicit workspace. Records only the authenticated user's acceptance. Repeating the same document acceptance returns the original receipt without another audit record. This natural operation identity supplies deduplication. A superseded or unpublished version returns legal_version_not_current.

200.description: Acceptance receipt, including an identical replay

get.summary: List the authenticated member's acceptance history for a workspace
get.description: Returns the earliest acceptance per document kind for the calling user in the explicit workspace. Members can only ever see their own rows; non-members receive workspace_membership_required. This is the single server truth both the re-accept gate and the go-live checklist read.

200.description: Acceptance history (empty array when nothing accepted)

post.description: Trusted bridge contract, not native vendor signature support. The bridge signs timestamp + dot + raw body using the provider-specific encrypted callback_hmac_secret. HMAC-SHA256 is lowercase hex. Timestamps permit five minutes of clock skew. Raw bodies are limited to 64 KiB. Generic HTTP and Africa's Talking payload mappings are supported. Identical bodies deduplicate within the provider. Accepted evidence may remain pending until a provider message ID is correlated.

202.description: Receipt evidence persisted or already recorded

401.description: Invalid signature, timestamp or callback configuration

post.description: Returns the same accepted response for unknown or inactive accounts. Codes expire after five minutes. Resends require 60 seconds; at most five requests per account per 30 minutes and ten per source IP per minute. Delivery failures invalidate the code without revealing account existence.

202.description: Request accepted without disclosing account existence

post.summary: Complete email login or continue to required two-factor authentication
post.description: Codes are single-use and permit at most five guesses. A successful email code does not bypass an enabled authenticator.

post.summary: Send a verification code for the authenticated session user
post.description: Requires a bearer session. Codes expire in ten minutes. Requests have a sixty-second cooldown.

post.summary: Consume the authenticated user's email verification code

post.description: Live purchases only. The prospective fee counts toward the workspace spend cap (402 on excess). Mixed-currency fees require a positive source-to-workspace FX rate dated within the previous seven UTC calendar days; unavailable FX returns 503 and rolls back both assignment and fee. Browser owner/admin sessions require enabled TOTP and explicit X-Workspace-ID and X-Environment. No recent-factor timestamp claim is made. Idempotency-Key is required; exact normalized requests replay the original Number snapshot and changed requests return 409. An unavailable or redacted purchase snapshot also returns 409. Current role or key scope and revocation or expiry are rechecked after locks. API keys remain bound to their stored workspace and environment. See docs/frontend-contract.md for operation roles and workspace-global resources.

error_code.description: Safe customer classification. Submission reasons include recipient_opted_out, provider_risk_hold, provider_invalid_sender, invalid_recipient, unsupported_destination, provider_insufficient_balance, provider_no_route, provider_gateway_rejected, provider_unauthorized, provider_invalid_request, and provider_rejected. Opt-out, risk hold, invalid recipient, and invalid request block retry and fallback. Other definitive rejections use only an already authorized eligible fallback. Unknown submissions never retry automatically. DLR failures use delivery_failed or delivery_expired; these describe the outcome and do not assert an unverified carrier-specific cause. Raw provider errors are never returned.
